points: Everyday examples of chemical change: milk left at room temperature in summer, iron tawa/pan/nail left in humid air (rusting), fermentation of grapes, cooking of food, digestion of food and respiration.
In all of these, the nature and identity of the starting substance changes. Whenever a chemical change occurs, a chemical reaction has taken place.
Activity 1.1: a clean magnesium ribbon burns in air with a dazzling white flame and changes into a white powder, magnesium oxide (MgO).
Activity 1.2: lead nitrate solution + potassium iodide solution gives a yellow precipitate of lead iodide.
Activity 1.3: zinc granules + dilute HCl or H₂SO₄ give bubbles of hydrogen gas, and the flask becomes warm.
A chemical reaction can be recognised by any of these observations: change in state, change in colour, evolution of a gas, change in temperature.
A word-equation writes a reaction in short form: Magnesium + Oxygen → Magnesium oxide.
Reactants are the substances that undergo chemical change; they are written on the left-hand side (LHS). Products are the new substances formed; they are written on the right-hand side (RHS).
A plus sign (+) separates two reactants or two products. The arrow points towards the products and shows the direction of the reaction.
A chemical equation uses chemical formulae instead of words, e.g. Mg + O₂ → MgO.
If the number of atoms of each element is not the same on both sides, the equation is unbalanced and is called a skeletal chemical equation.
Law of conservation of mass: mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction. So the number of atoms of each element must be the same before and after the reaction.
Example of a balanced equation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂ (Zn 1, H 2, S 1, O 4 on both sides).
Steps to balance Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂ (hit-and-trial method):
Step I: draw boxes around each formula; never change anything inside a box, i.e. never change a formula (write 4H₂O, not H₂O₄ or (H₂O)₄).
Step II: list the number of atoms of each element on both sides.
Step III: start with the compound having the maximum number of atoms (Fe₃O₄) and the element with most atoms in it (oxygen): Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂.
Step IV: balance hydrogen: Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.
Step V: balance the remaining element, iron: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.
Step VI: count atoms on both sides again to check that the equation is balanced.
Step VII: add physical-state symbols: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) aqueous solution in water. 3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g). Here (g) with water shows steam is used.

Reaction conditions such as temperature, pressure or catalyst are written above/below the arrow, e.g. CO(g) + 2H₂(g) → CH₃OH(l) at 340 atm; 6CO₂(aq) + 12H₂O(l) → C₆H₁₂O₆(aq) + 6O₂(aq) + 6H₂O(l) in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll (photosynthesis).
A reaction in which a single product is formed from two or more reactants.
Activity 1.4: quick lime reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime, releasing a large amount of heat: CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq) + Heat.

Whitewashing: a solution of slaked lime reacts slowly with CO₂ in air to form a thin layer of calcium carbonate in 2-3 days, giving a shiny finish: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l). Marble is also CaCO₃.
Other examples: burning of coal, C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g); formation of water, 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l).
Exothermic reactions release heat along with the formation of products.
Examples: burning of natural gas, CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g); respiration, C₆H₁₂O₆(aq) + 6O₂(aq) → 6CO₂(aq) + 6H₂O(l) + energy; decomposition of vegetable matter into compost.
Respiration is exothermic: carbohydrates in food (rice, potatoes, bread) are broken down into glucose, which combines with oxygen in our cells to give energy.
Endothermic reactions absorb energy (heat, light or electricity). Decomposition reactions are generally endothermic because energy is needed to break the reactant down.
A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down to give simpler products. It is the opposite of a combination reaction.

Thermal decomposition (by heat): Activity 1.5 - green ferrous sulphate crystals lose water and change colour on heating, and a smell of burning sulphur is noticed: 2FeSO₄(s) → Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g) (on heating).
Limestone decomposes on heating: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g). Quick lime (CaO) is used in the manufacture of cement.
Activity 1.6 - heating lead nitrate gives brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide: 2Pb(NO₃)₂(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g).

Electrolytic decomposition (by electricity): Activity 1.7 - electrolysis of water, 2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g). The volume of gas collected at the cathode (hydrogen) is double the volume at the anode (oxygen). Hydrogen burns with a pop sound; oxygen relights a glowing splinter.

Photolytic decomposition (by light): Activity 1.8 - white silver chloride turns grey in sunlight: 2AgCl(s) → 2Ag(s) + Cl₂(g). Silver bromide behaves similarly: 2AgBr(s) → 2Ag(s) + Br₂(g). These reactions are used in black and white photography.
A more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
Activity 1.9: iron nails dipped in copper sulphate solution become brownish and the blue colour of the solution fades: Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s).
Other examples: Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s); Pb(s) + CuCl₂(aq) → PbCl₂(aq) + Cu(s).
Zinc and lead are more reactive than copper, so they displace copper from its compounds.
A reaction in which there is an exchange of ions between the reactants.
Activity 1.10: sodium sulphate solution + barium chloride solution gives a white insoluble substance, barium sulphate: Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq).
An insoluble substance formed in a reaction is called a precipitate. Any reaction that produces a precipitate is a precipitation reaction.
Lead nitrate + potassium iodide (Activity 1.2) is also a double displacement reaction giving a yellow precipitate of lead iodide: Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI(aq) → PbI₂(s) + 2KNO₃(aq).
Activity 1.11: heating copper powder in air forms a black coating of copper(II) oxide: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO (on heating).
Passing hydrogen over hot CuO turns the black coating brown again as copper is obtained: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O (on heating).
Oxidation: a substance gains oxygen or loses hydrogen. Reduction: a substance loses oxygen or gains hydrogen.
In CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, copper(II) oxide is reduced to copper and hydrogen is oxidised to water.
Reactions in which one reactant is oxidised and the other is reduced are called oxidation-reduction or redox reactions.
Other examples: ZnO + C → Zn + CO (ZnO reduced, C oxidised); MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂ (MnO₂ reduced, HCl oxidised).

summary.topic: Effects of oxidation in everyday life
points: Corrosion: when a metal is attacked by substances around it such as moisture and acids, it corrodes. Examples: reddish-brown coating on iron (rusting), black coating on silver, green coating on copper.
Corrosion causes damage to car bodies, bridges, iron railings, ships and all objects made of metals, especially iron. Huge amounts of money are spent every year to replace damaged iron.
Rancidity: when fats and oils are oxidised, they become rancid and their smell and taste change.

Rancidity is prevented by adding antioxidants to foods containing fats and oils, and by storing food in air-tight containers. Chips packets are flushed with an inert gas such as nitrogen to prevent oxidation.

key_points: Signs of a chemical reaction: change in state, change in colour, evolution of a gas, change in temperature.
Law of conservation of mass: mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; atoms of each element are equal on both sides of a balanced equation.
Skeletal equation = unbalanced chemical equation. Balancing method used in NCERT = hit-and-trial method.
Never change the formula of a substance while balancing; change only the coefficients.
State symbols: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas, (aq) aqueous.
3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g)
Combination: A + B → AB. CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq) + Heat (quick lime → slaked lime).
Whitewash: Ca(OH)₂ + CO₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O (shiny finish after 2-3 days; marble is CaCO₃).
Decomposition: AB → A + B; types - thermal (heat), electrolytic (electricity), photolytic (light).
2FeSO₄ → Fe₂O₃ + SO₂ + SO₃ (green crystals change colour; smell of burning sulphur).
CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (quick lime used for cement).
2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂ (brown fumes of NO₂).
Electrolysis of water: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂; hydrogen volume is twice that of oxygen.
2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ and 2AgBr → 2Ag + Br₂ in sunlight; used in black and white photography.
Displacement: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu (blue solution fades, nail turns brown).
Double displacement: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄↓ (white ppt) + 2NaCl; Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂↓ (yellow ppt) + 2KNO₃.
Precipitate: insoluble solid formed in a reaction; such reactions are precipitation reactions.
Oxidation = gain of oxygen / loss of hydrogen. Reduction = loss of oxygen / gain of hydrogen.
Redox: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O; ZnO + C → Zn + CO; MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂.
Exothermic reactions give out heat (respiration, burning of natural gas, composting); decomposition reactions are generally endothermic.
Corrosion: rust on iron (reddish brown), black coating on silver, green coating on copper.
Rancidity: oxidation of fats and oils; prevented by antioxidants, air-tight containers and nitrogen flushing.

one_mark.question: Which of the statements about the reaction 2PbO(s) + C(s) → 2Pb(s) + CO₂(g) are incorrect? Statement 1: Lead is getting reduced. Statement 2: Carbon dioxide is getting oxidised. Statement 3: Carbon is getting oxidised. Statement 4: Lead oxide is getting reduced.
one_mark.answer: (a) 1 and 2. Lead is a product (it is PbO that gets reduced), and CO₂ is a product formed by the oxidation of carbon.

Iron salt and water are produced

Substances that undergo chemical change in a reaction are called ________.
An unbalanced chemical equation is called a ________ chemical equation.
The method of balancing used by making trials with the smallest whole-number coefficients is called the ________ method.
The state symbol (aq) stands for ________.
one_mark.answer: aqueous (present as a solution in water)

one_mark.question: Calcium oxide is commonly called ________ and calcium hydroxide is called ________.
Magnesium ribbon burns with a dazzling ________ flame.
An insoluble substance formed during a reaction is called a ________.
Decomposition of silver bromide in sunlight is used in ________ photography.
Gain of hydrogen by a substance is called ________.
Oxidation of fats and oils resulting in a change in their smell and taste is called ________.

one_mark.question: While balancing an equation, the formula H₂O can be changed to H₂O₂ to balance oxygen.
one_mark.answer: False. Formulae must never be changed; only coefficients (e.g. 2H₂O) can be changed.

one_mark.question: Zinc can displace copper from copper sulphate solution.
one_mark.answer: True. Zinc is more reactive than copper.

one_mark.question: Respiration is an endothermic process.
one_mark.answer: False. Respiration is an exothermic process; it releases energy.

Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air?
one_mark.answer: To remove the protective layer of magnesium oxide (and dirt) on its surface so that magnesium burns readily in air.

What change in colour is observed when white silver chloride is left in sunlight?
one_mark.answer: It turns grey, because silver chloride decomposes into silver and chlorine.

one_mark.question: Why does the colour of copper sulphate solution change when an iron nail is dipped in it?
one_mark.answer: Iron displaces copper from copper sulphate to form ferrous sulphate (light green), so the blue colour fades: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu.

one_mark.question: Name the product formed when quick lime is used to make cement after heating limestone.
one_mark.answer: Calcium oxide (quick lime), formed by CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.

one_mark.question: Why do we apply paint on iron articles?
one_mark.answer: Paint prevents moisture and air from coming in contact with iron, so it prevents rusting (corrosion).

one_mark.question: Oil and fat containing food items are flushed with nitrogen. Why?
one_mark.answer: Nitrogen is an inert gas; it prevents oxidation of fats and oils, so the food does not become rancid.

one_mark.question: Assertion (A): A chemical equation must be balanced. Reason (R): Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
one_mark.answer: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

one_mark.question: Assertion (A): The reaction CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ is a combination reaction. Reason (R): Heat is released in this reaction.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
one_mark.answer: (b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A. It is a combination reaction because a single product is formed from two reactants.

one_mark.question: Assertion (A): In the reaction ZnO + C → Zn + CO, zinc oxide is reduced. Reason (R): Zinc oxide loses oxygen in this reaction.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
one_mark.answer: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

one_mark.question: Assertion (A): Silver articles become black after some time when exposed to air. Reason (R): Silver is oxidised by oxygen to form a white oxide.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
one_mark.answer: (c) A is true but R is false. Silver corrodes and gets a black coating; it is not a white oxide.

short_answer.question: What is a balanced chemical equation? Why should chemical equations be balanced?
short_answer.answer:
- A balanced chemical equation has an equal number of atoms of each element on both sides (reactants and products).
- Equations must be balanced to satisfy the law of conservation of mass: mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

short_answer.question: Translate into a balanced chemical equation: Hydrogen sulphide gas burns in air to give water and sulphur dioxide.
short_answer.answer: 2H₂S(g) + 3O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l) + 2SO₂(g)

short_answer.question: Write the balanced chemical equations for: (i) Barium chloride + Aluminium sulphate → Barium sulphate + Aluminium chloride (ii) Sodium + Water → Sodium hydroxide + Hydrogen
short_answer.answer:
- (i) 3BaCl₂ + Al₂(SO₄)₃ → 3BaSO₄ + 2AlCl₃
- (ii) 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂

short_answer.question: Write balanced chemical equations with state symbols: (i) Solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulphate in water react to give insoluble barium sulphate and a solution of sodium chloride. (ii) Sodium hydroxide solution reacts with hydrochloric acid solution to produce sodium chloride solution and water.
short_answer.answer:
- (i) BaCl₂(aq) + Na₂SO₄(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq)
- (ii) NaOH(aq) + HCl(aq) → NaCl(aq) + H₂O(l)

short_answer.question: A solution of a substance 'X' is used for whitewashing. (i) Name the substance 'X' and write its formula. (ii) Write the reaction of 'X' with water.
short_answer.answer:
- (i) X is calcium oxide (quick lime), CaO.
- (ii) CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq) + Heat. The calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) solution formed is used for whitewashing.

short_answer.question: Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction? Explain.
short_answer.answer:
- During digestion, carbohydrates are broken down into glucose.
- Glucose combines with oxygen in our cells and releases energy: C₆H₁₂O₆(aq) + 6O₂(aq) → 6CO₂(aq) + 6H₂O(l) + energy.
- Since energy is released, respiration is an exothermic reaction.

short_answer.question: Why are decomposition reactions called the opposite of combination reactions? Write equations for these reactions.
short_answer.answer:
- In a combination reaction, two or more reactants combine to form a single product, e.g. CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.
- In a decomposition reaction, a single reactant breaks down into two or more simpler products, e.g. CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ (on heating).
- So the two are opposite processes.

short_answer.question: Why does the colour of copper sulphate solution change when an iron nail is dipped in it?
short_answer.answer:
- Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate solution: Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s).
- Ferrous sulphate formed is light green, so the blue colour of the solution fades, and a brown coating of copper forms on the nail.

short_answer.question: Explain the following in terms of gain or loss of oxygen with two examples each: (a) Oxidation (b) Reduction
short_answer.answer:
- (a) Oxidation is gain of oxygen. Examples: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO; in CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, H₂ is oxidised to H₂O.
- (b) Reduction is loss of oxygen. Examples: in CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, CuO is reduced to Cu; in ZnO + C → Zn + CO, ZnO is reduced to Zn.

short_answer.question: A shiny brown coloured element 'X' on heating in air becomes black in colour. Name the element 'X' and the black coloured compound formed.
short_answer.answer:
- X is copper (Cu); the black compound is copper(II) oxide (CuO).
- 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO (on heating)

short_answer.question: Explain the following terms with one example each: (a) Corrosion (b) Rancidity
short_answer.answer:
- (a) Corrosion: a metal is attacked by substances around it such as moisture and acids and gets damaged. Example: rusting of iron (reddish-brown coating).
- (b) Rancidity: fats and oils get oxidised and their smell and taste change. Example: chips or butter left open for a long time taste and smell bad.

short_answer.question: What does one mean by exothermic and endothermic reactions? Give examples.
short_answer.answer:
- Exothermic reactions release heat. Example: CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g) + heat (burning of natural gas).
- Endothermic reactions absorb energy. Example: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g) on heating; 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂ in sunlight.

short_answer.question: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before it is burnt in air? Write the balanced equation for the reaction and state what you observe.
short_answer.answer:
- Magnesium ribbon has a layer of magnesium oxide on its surface which slows down burning; cleaning with sandpaper removes this layer so that magnesium burns readily.
- Equation: 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s)
- Observation: it burns with a dazzling white flame and changes into a white powder (magnesium oxide).

short_answer.question: Balance the equation Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂ step by step and write it with state symbols.
short_answer.answer:
- Oxygen: 1 on LHS, 4 on RHS, so write 4H₂O: Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂.
- Hydrogen: 8 on LHS, 2 on RHS, so write 4H₂: Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.
- Iron: 1 on LHS, 3 on RHS, so write 3Fe: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.
- With state symbols: 3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g) (water is used as steam).

short_answer.question: Write balanced chemical equations for the following and identify the type of each reaction: (a) Potassium bromide(aq) + Barium iodide(aq) → Potassium iodide(aq) + Barium bromide(s) (b) Zinc carbonate(s) → Zinc oxide(s) + Carbon dioxide(g) (c) Hydrogen(g) + Chlorine(g) → Hydrogen chloride(g) (d) Magnesium(s) + Hydrochloric acid(aq) → Magnesium chloride(aq) + Hydrogen(g)
short_answer.answer:
- (a) 2KBr(aq) + BaI₂(aq) → 2KI(aq) + BaBr₂(s): double displacement reaction
- (b) ZnCO₃(s) → ZnO(s) + CO₂(g): decomposition reaction
- (c) H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g): combination reaction
- (d) Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g): displacement reaction

short_answer.question: Write the balanced chemical equation for the following and identify the type of reaction in each case: (a) Thermit reaction, iron(III) oxide reacts with aluminium and gives molten iron and aluminium oxide. (b) Magnesium ribbon is burnt in an atmosphere of nitrogen gas to form solid magnesium nitride. (c) Chlorine gas is passed in an aqueous potassium iodide solution to form potassium chloride solution and solid iodine.
short_answer.answer:
- (a) Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(l): displacement reaction (also redox)
- (b) 3Mg(s) + N₂(g) → Mg₃N₂(s): combination reaction
- (c) Cl₂(g) + 2KI(aq) → 2KCl(aq) + I₂(s): displacement reaction

short_answer.question: Write one equation each for decomposition reactions where energy is supplied in the form of heat, light and electricity.
short_answer.answer:
- Heat (thermal decomposition): CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g)
- Light (photolytic decomposition): 2AgCl(s) → 2Ag(s) + Cl₂(g) in sunlight
- Electricity (electrolytic decomposition): 2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g)

short_answer.question: What is the difference between displacement and double displacement reactions? Write equations for these reactions.
short_answer.answer:
- In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. Example: Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s).
- In a double displacement reaction, two compounds exchange their ions. Example: Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq).
- In displacement only one element is replaced; in double displacement both compounds exchange their parts.

short_answer.question: In the refining of silver, the recovery of silver from silver nitrate solution involves displacement by copper metal. Write down the reaction involved.
short_answer.answer:
- Copper is more reactive than silver, so it displaces silver from silver nitrate solution.
- Cu(s) + 2AgNO₃(aq) → Cu(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2Ag(s)
- The solution turns blue due to copper nitrate and silver metal is deposited.

short_answer.question: What do you mean by a precipitation reaction? Explain by giving examples.
short_answer.answer:
- A reaction that produces an insoluble substance (precipitate) is called a precipitation reaction.
- Example 1: Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq); a white precipitate of barium sulphate forms.
- Example 2: Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI(aq) → PbI₂(s) + 2KNO₃(aq); a yellow precipitate of lead iodide forms.
- Both are double displacement reactions.

short_answer.question: Identify the substances that are oxidised and the substances that are reduced: (i) 4Na(s) + O₂(g) → 2Na₂O(s) (ii) CuO(s) + H₂(g) → Cu(s) + H₂O(l) (iii) MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂
short_answer.answer:
- (i) Na is oxidised (gains oxygen); O₂ is reduced.
- (ii) H₂ is oxidised to H₂O; CuO is reduced to Cu.
- (iii) HCl is oxidised (loses hydrogen) to Cl₂; MnO₂ is reduced (loses oxygen) to MnCl₂.

short_answer.question: Why is silver chloride stored in dark coloured bottles? Explain with an equation.
short_answer.answer:
- Silver chloride decomposes in the presence of sunlight: 2AgCl(s) → 2Ag(s) + Cl₂(g).
- White silver chloride turns grey as silver is formed.
- Coloured (dark) bottles cut off light and prevent this photolytic decomposition.

short_answer.question: What is observed when lead nitrate is heated? Write the equation and name the type of reaction.
short_answer.answer:
- Brown fumes of nitrogen dioxide are given off and a yellowish residue of lead oxide remains.
- 2Pb(NO₃)₂(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g) (on heating)
- It is a thermal decomposition reaction.

short_answer.question: What are the effects of corrosion? How can rancidity of food be prevented?
short_answer.answer:
- Corrosion damages car bodies, bridges, iron railings, ships and all objects made of metals, especially iron; a huge amount of money is spent each year to replace damaged iron.
- Rancidity can be prevented by adding antioxidants to food containing fats and oils.
- Storing food in air-tight containers and flushing packets (e.g. chips) with nitrogen also slows oxidation.

long_answer.question: What is a chemical equation? Explain the steps of balancing a chemical equation by the hit-and-trial method, taking the reaction of iron with steam as an example. Why do we write state symbols and reaction conditions?
long_answer.answer:
A chemical equation represents a chemical reaction using the formulae of reactants and products. Reactant: iron and steam; products: iron(II, III) oxide and hydrogen.
- Skeletal equation: Fe + H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂.
- Step I: draw boxes around each formula; do not change anything inside the boxes.
- Step II: list atoms on each side: Fe 1 and 3, H 2 and 2, O 1 and 4.
- Step III: start with the compound having most atoms (Fe₃O₄) and its element with most atoms (O). Put 4 before H₂O: Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + H₂.
- Step IV: balance H: 8 on LHS, so put 4 before H₂: Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.
- Step V: balance Fe: put 3 before Fe: 3Fe + 4H₂O → Fe₃O₄ + 4H₂.
- Step VI: check: Fe 3 = 3, H 8 = 8, O 4 = 4. The equation is balanced.
- Step VII: add state symbols: 3Fe(s) + 4H₂O(g) → Fe₃O₄(s) + 4H₂(g).
- State symbols (s, l, g, aq) make the equation more informative by giving the physical state of each substance; conditions such as temperature, pressure, catalyst or sunlight are written above/below the arrow, e.g. CO(g) + 2H₂(g) → CH₃OH(l) at 340 atm.

long_answer.question: What is a decomposition reaction? Describe with equations the three ways in which energy can be supplied for decomposition. Mention one use of each type.
long_answer.answer:
A decomposition reaction is one in which a single reactant breaks down to give simpler products. These reactions generally need energy, so they are endothermic.
- Thermal decomposition (heat): heating ferrous sulphate - green crystals change colour with a smell of burning sulphur: 2FeSO₄(s) → Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g). Heating limestone: CaCO₃(s) → CaO(s) + CO₂(g); the quick lime formed is used in the manufacture of cement. Heating lead nitrate gives brown fumes: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂.
- Electrolytic decomposition (electricity): passing current through water: 2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g). Hydrogen collects at the cathode and oxygen at the anode; the volume of hydrogen is double that of oxygen. Used to obtain hydrogen and oxygen.
- Photolytic decomposition (light): white silver chloride turns grey in sunlight: 2AgCl(s) → 2Ag(s) + Cl₂(g); similarly 2AgBr(s) → 2Ag(s) + Br₂(g). Used in black and white photography.

long_answer.question: Describe an activity to show the electrolysis of water. Write the equation, state the observations and how you would test the gases produced.
long_answer.answer:
- Take a plastic mug, drill two holes at its base and fit rubber stoppers in them. Insert carbon electrodes in the stoppers and connect them to a 6 V battery.
- Fill the mug with water so that the electrodes are immersed, and add a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid.
- Take two test tubes filled with water and invert them over the two carbon electrodes.
- Switch on the current and leave the apparatus undisturbed for some time.
- Observation: bubbles form at both electrodes and displace water in the test tubes. The volume of gas collected over the cathode (negative electrode) is double that over the anode.
- Equation: 2H₂O(l) → 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) (electric current).
- Test: bring a burning candle close to the mouth of each tube. Hydrogen burns with a pop sound; oxygen makes a glowing splinter/candle burn brighter.
- This is an electrolytic decomposition reaction.

long_answer.question: Explain displacement and double displacement reactions with activities and equations. How is a precipitation reaction related to them?
long_answer.answer:
Displacement reaction:
- A more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
- Activity: dip clean iron nails in copper sulphate solution for about 20 minutes. The nails become brownish and the blue colour of the solution fades: Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → FeSO₄(aq) + Cu(s).
- Other examples: Zn(s) + CuSO₄(aq) → ZnSO₄(aq) + Cu(s); Pb(s) + CuCl₂(aq) → PbCl₂(aq) + Cu(s). Zinc and lead are more reactive than copper.
Double displacement reaction:
- There is an exchange of ions between the reactants.
- Activity: mix sodium sulphate solution with barium chloride solution. A white insoluble substance, barium sulphate, forms: Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) → BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl(aq).
Precipitation reaction:
- The insoluble substance formed is a precipitate, and any reaction that produces a precipitate is a precipitation reaction.
- Most double displacement reactions in solution, like the one above and Pb(NO₃)₂(aq) + 2KI(aq) → PbI₂(s) (yellow) + 2KNO₃(aq), are precipitation reactions.

long_answer.question: What are oxidation and reduction? Explain with an activity why oxidation and reduction occur together (redox reaction). Give two more examples.
long_answer.answer:
- Oxidation: gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen by a substance. Reduction: loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen by a substance.
- Activity: heat about 1 g copper powder in a china dish. The brown surface becomes coated with black copper(II) oxide because copper combines with oxygen: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO (copper is oxidised).
- Now pass hydrogen gas over the heated black material. The black coating turns brown again because CuO loses oxygen: CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O.
- In this reaction CuO is reduced to Cu and at the same time H₂ is oxidised to H₂O. One reactant gets oxidised while the other gets reduced, so it is called an oxidation-reduction or redox reaction.
- Example 1: ZnO + C → Zn + CO; ZnO is reduced and C is oxidised.
- Example 2: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + 2H₂O + Cl₂; MnO₂ is reduced and HCl is oxidised.

long_answer.question: What is a combination reaction? Explain with the reaction of quick lime and water, and describe how whitewashing gives a shiny finish. Is this reaction exothermic? Give other examples of exothermic reactions.
long_answer.answer:
- A combination reaction is one in which a single product is formed from two or more reactants.
- Activity: add water slowly to a small amount of calcium oxide (quick lime) in a beaker. The beaker becomes hot. CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq) + Heat. Calcium hydroxide is slaked lime.
- Whitewashing: slaked lime solution applied to walls reacts slowly with carbon dioxide in air, forming a thin layer of calcium carbonate in two to three days, which gives a shiny finish: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + CO₂(g) → CaCO₃(s) + H₂O(l). Marble also has the formula CaCO₃.
- Since a large amount of heat is released, the reaction of quick lime with water is exothermic.
- Other combination reactions: C(s) + O₂(g) → CO₂(g); 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l).
- Other exothermic reactions: burning of natural gas, CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(g); respiration, C₆H₁₂O₆(aq) + 6O₂(aq) → 6CO₂(aq) + 6H₂O(l) + energy; decomposition of vegetable matter into compost.

long_answer.question: Explain corrosion and rancidity as effects of oxidation in everyday life. Describe their harmful effects and how they can be prevented.
long_answer.answer:
Corrosion:
- When a metal is attacked by substances around it such as moisture and acids, it is said to corrode.
- Examples: iron gets a reddish-brown coating (rust), silver gets a black coating and copper gets a green coating.
- Harmful effects: it damages car bodies, bridges, iron railings, ships and all objects made of metals, especially iron. A large amount of money is spent each year to replace damaged iron.
- Prevention: painting, oiling or greasing iron articles keeps air and moisture away.
Rancidity:
- When fats and oils are oxidised, they become rancid and their smell and taste change.
- Harmful effect: food becomes unpleasant and unfit to eat.
- Prevention: antioxidants are added to food containing fats and oils; food is kept in air-tight containers; chips packets are flushed with nitrogen, an inert gas, so that the chips do not get oxidised.
